\documentclass{beamer}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\setbeamertemplate{navigation symbols}{}
\setbeamertemplate{footline}[frame number]

\begin{document}

\begin{frame}{Deriving the Range}
  A projectile leaves the ground at speed $v_0$ and angle $\theta$.
  \pause
  \begin{equation*}
    t_{\text{flight}} = \frac{2 v_0 \sin\theta}{g}
  \end{equation*}
  \pause
  \begin{equation*}
    R = v_0 \cos\theta \; t_{\text{flight}} = \frac{v_0^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}
  \end{equation*}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Checking the Result}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item<1-> The range is largest at $\theta = 45^\circ$.
    \item<2-> At $\theta = 0$ the range is zero.
    \item<3-> The maximum is $R_{\max} = v_0^2 / g$.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\end{document}
